# Swagger UI Theming

How the API documentation page (`/api/docs/ui`) is styled, and how to keep it working when Swagger UI changes.

## Where it lives

| File | Contents |
|------|----------|
| `server/swagger-ui.ts` | The whole page: markup, styles, the theme script, the pinned asset URLs and their SRI hashes |
| `server/routes.ts` | Serves `swaggerUiHtml` at `/api/docs/ui` with the Swagger UI CSP and `Cache-Control: no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate` |
| `server/openapi.ts` | The OpenAPI document; its examples are generated by the API at startup |
| `server/csp-config.ts` | `buildSwaggerUICSP()`: the route's CSP (adds `cdn.jsdelivr.net` and inline scripts) |

## Design

**One palette, two themes.** `:root` defines color tokens copied from the web app (`client/src/index.css`): `--background`, `--foreground`, `--card`, `--border`, `--input`, `--muted`, `--muted-foreground`, `--primary`, `--primary-foreground`, `--secondary`, `--destructive`, `--success`. `html.dark` redefines only the tokens. Every rule uses tokens, so the two themes can't drift apart. A test (`tests/integration/api-endpoints.test.ts`, "should use the web app's color tokens in both themes") reads nine of these tokens from `client/src/index.css` in both themes, `--background`, `--foreground`, `--card`, `--border`, `--muted-foreground`, `--primary`, `--primary-foreground`, `--destructive`, and `--success`, and fails if the docs page's `:root` or `html.dark` value for any of them differs. It does not check `--input`, `--muted`, or `--secondary`, which can drift unnoticed.

**Fixed accent colors.** HTTP method badges use `--method-get` (#2563eb), `--method-post` (#047857), `--method-put`, `--method-patch`, `--method-delete`, `--method-other`. They are the same in both themes and dark enough for white text at 4.5:1 or better. Each operation also gets a 4px left border in its method color. `--success` (green text such as "Controls Accept header.") and `--copy-bg` (copy and download buttons) do change per theme.

**Overriding Swagger's hard-coded colors.** Swagger UI's CSS hard-codes dark text (mostly `#3b4151`), light surfaces, and generic fonts on specific selectors. `server/swagger-ui.ts` keeps those selectors as lists (`TEXT_SELECTORS`, `MUTED_TEXT_SELECTORS`, `SURFACE_SELECTORS`, `SANS_SELECTORS`, `MONO_SELECTORS`) taken from the pinned `swagger-ui.css`, and points each at a token. Because the overrides match Swagger's own selectors, plain CSS wins without `!important`. The one exception is code panel backgrounds, which Swagger's highlighter sets inline.

**Code highlighting.** Swagger UI's built-in highlight themes do the token coloring: `idea` in light mode, `tomorrow-night` in dark. Our CSS sets only the panel background, border, and the base text color (plain blocks such as Request URL and Response headers get no inline color, and Swagger's default is white).

**Fonts.** Inter and JetBrains Mono, loaded from Google Fonts like the web app.

**Layout.** `BaseLayout` (no Swagger top bar), so the 268 KB standalone preset isn't loaded. Swagger's `.wrapper` padding is removed so the info, servers, operations, and schemas cards line up with the page header.

**Theme switching.** A head script applies the saved theme (`localStorage` key `theme`, shared with the web app; default light) before anything paints. The toggle and the cross-tab `storage` listener call `render(theme)`, which sets the class and re-mounts Swagger UI on a fresh node with the matching highlight theme. There is no page reload, and no script repaints elements after rendering. Icons switch via CSS (`html.dark #theme-toggle .sun-icon`).

**Deep links.** `deepLinking: true`, with explicit `operationId`s (`generateNetworkPlan`, `getDeploymentTiers`, `getHealth`, ...) so links read `#/Kubernetes/generateNetworkPlan`. Swagger's generated IDs contain underscores, which its deep-link parser treats as deprecated whitespace escapes.

## Updating Swagger UI

Assets load from `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/swagger-ui-dist@<version>` with `sha384` Subresource Integrity; a stale hash makes the browser refuse the file. To upgrade:

1. Set `SWAGGER_UI_VERSION` in `server/swagger-ui.ts`.
2. Recompute both hashes and replace `SRI.css` and `SRI.bundle`:
   ```bash
   V=5.33.1   # the new version
   for f in swagger-ui.css swagger-ui-bundle.js; do
     curl -sSfL "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/swagger-ui-dist@$V/$f" -o "$f"
     echo "$f sha384-$(openssl dgst -sha384 -binary "$f" | openssl base64 -A)"
   done
   ```
3. Regenerate the selector lists from the new `swagger-ui.css`. Rules setting `color:#3b4151` (and other dark greys) feed `TEXT_SELECTORS`; light `background` values feed `SURFACE_SELECTORS`; `font-family:sans-serif` and `monospace` feed `SANS_SELECTORS` and `MONO_SELECTORS`. Skip the Tachyons helper classes (`.black`, `.bg-white`, `.hover-*`, ...) and the `json-schema-2020-12` viewer, which an OpenAPI 3.0 document never renders.
4. Check that `idea` and `tomorrow-night` still exist in `swagger-ui-bundle.js` (`grep -c 'idea:{' swagger-ui-bundle.js`).
5. Look at the page in both themes: the info card, servers, an expanded operation after "Try it out" and "Execute" (curl, request URL, response body, response headers), and the Schemas section. Check the browser console for errors and CSP violations.

## Testing

- `tests/integration/api-endpoints.test.ts` ("Swagger UI Presentation"): token parity with the web app (the nine tokens listed under [Design](#design)), method badge colors, pinned assets with SRI (exactly two CDN tags, no standalone preset), favicon, theme toggle without reload, no repaint script, header and footer.
- `tests/integration/swagger-ui-csp-middleware.test.ts`: the route's CSP.
- `tests/integration/swagger-ui-theming.test.ts`: the same page served by an in-process server the test starts itself, so it always runs (no `npm run dev` needed).
- `npm run smoke` (after `npm run build`; CI runs both): the production bundle serves `/api/docs/ui` with exactly two CDN tags, each with a `sha384` integrity hash, under a CSP that allows `cdn.jsdelivr.net`. It checks that the hashes are present, not that they match the files; a wrong hash only shows up in the browser (step 5 above).
- Visual checks: render the page in headless Chrome in both themes (set `localStorage.theme`, open `#/Kubernetes/generateNetworkPlan`, choose "Try it out" and "Execute") and review screenshots. There is no committed visual-regression suite.

## Known limitations

- Without JavaScript, Swagger UI doesn't render at all (it is a client-side app); the header, footer, and light theme still show.
- The Schemas section shows primitive properties collapsed (`[...]`) until clicked. That is Swagger's own behavior; `defaultModelExpandDepth: 2` expands them in each operation's Schema tab.
